job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

response.passage: In our chemistry lab, we performed experiments to understand the properties of various elements. First, we took a piece of sodium and easily sliced it with a knife, proving that not all metals are hard solids. Next, we tested graphite, a form of carbon, and found it conducts electricity, showing that non-metals can indeed be conductive. We then placed a strip of copper into a solution of silver nitrate. The copper displaced the silver, not because it is heavier, but because it is more reactive in the chemical series. We also observed that when magnesium reacts with hydrochloric acid, it forms a new substance, magnesium chloride, rather than just disappearing or turning into liquid. Finally, we examined a rusted iron nail and a tarnished copper wire. We concluded that corrosion is a chemical process affecting many metals, not just iron, and it creates a new chemical compound rather than being a simple layer of surface dirt.
response.summary: This experiment demonstrates that metals and non-metals have diverse properties that defy common assumptions. It highlights that chemical reactivity, conductivity, and corrosion are complex processes involving new substance formation.
